newsitem.title: USA: U.S. EPA keeps nitrogen dioxide standard.
newsitem.headline: U.S. EPA keeps nitrogen dioxide standard.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said on Friday it would keep its current air quality standards for nitrogen dioxide, produced mostly from vehicle exhaust and power plant emissions.
The EPA said it decided that current standard of 0.053 parts per million, measured as a national average, were adequate to proect public health and the environment.
No areas of the country have violated the standard for the past three years, the agency said.
But in a statement the EPA said it remained "concerned about the emissions of the this gas, which can contribute to other environmental problems, such as ground-level ozone (smog) and acid rain."

To fight these, the agency said it already has tightened tailpipe emissions standards for 1994-96 cars, required strict controls on large nitrogen dioxide (NO2) sources in areas that do not meet smog standards, and completed acid-rain rules for coal-fired utility boilers to cut NO2 emissions by 1.2 million tons annually by 2000.
The Clean Air Act requires the agency to review standards every five years for six air pollutants.
